Objective: Verify the post-reset default values (S_AXI_ARESETN=0) of all 17 registers (0x00..0x40), configuration output ports cfg_*_o, start_o, and irq_o.
Stimulus: Hold S_AXI_ARESETN=0 for 10 clock cycles, then deassert it to 1 and perform sequential AXI-Lite read transactions from address 0x00 to 0x40 (4-byte stride).
Checks: Verify that 0x24 (out_mode) defaults to 32'h0000_0001 (2'b01: INT8 mode); 0x40 (hw_version) = 32'h0006_0001; all other registers = 32'h0000_0000; start_o=0, irq_o=0, and S_AXI_RRESP=2'b00.
Expected_result: All 17 registers and cfg_*_o output wires match the post-reset design specification 100%; no bits contain X/Z values.
Notes: Note that r_out_mode_r defaults to 2'b01 (line 160) rather than 2'b00.
Golden_Reference_Rule: After reset: reg[0x24]==1, reg[0x40]==32'h00060001, all other regs == 0.
Bug_Injection_Target: Misconfiguring r_out_mode_r <= 2'b00 on reset or using an incorrect HW_VERSION constant -> TB reports FAIL on the very first test.
Pass_Criteria: 17/17 reads match default values; 0 X/Z errors.

Objective: Verify Read/Write (RW) capability and effective bit-width masking of all 15 configuration registers: 20-bit group (0x00..0x0C), 32-bit group (0x10..0x20, 0x28, 0x30..0x3C), and 2-bit group (0x24).
Stimulus: Sequentially write bit patterns 32'hFFFF_FFFF, 32'hAAAA_AAAA, 32'h5555_5555, and 32'h0000_0000 to each configuration register (excluding 0x2C and 0x40); after each write, read back via AXI-Lite and directly inspect the cfg_*_o output ports.
Checks: Verify that registers 0x00 (m_total), 0x04 (n_total), 0x08 (k_total), and 0x0C (k_dim) retain only the lower 20 bits [19:0] (upper 12 bits read back as 0); register 0x24 (out_mode) retains only the lower 2 bits [1:0] (upper 30 bits read back as 0); address/stride registers retain all 32 bits.
Expected_result: Data read back via S_AXI_RDATA and values on cfg_*_o ports match each register's bit-width mask 100%; no cross-register address aliasing occurs.
Notes: Verifies address decoding on axi_awaddr_r[7:2] and axi_araddr_r[7:2] across the entire register set.
Golden_Reference_Rule: RDATA(addr) == WDATA & mask(addr); cfg_port(addr) == WDATA & mask(addr).
Bug_Injection_Target: Typo in address decode 6'h0C..6'h0F or omitting zero-extension {{(32-DIM_W){1'b0}}, r_*_r} on readback -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: 100% of read/write operations and cfg_*_o ports match the bit-mask.

Objective: Verify Read-Only (RO) protection of the version register 0x40 (HW_VERSION) as well as status bits [3:1] (err, done_sticky, busy) and bit [0] (always reads as 0) of register 0x2C.
Stimulus: Attempt to write 32'hDEAD_BEEF and 32'h0000_0000 to 0x40; write 32'hFFFF_FFFE (bit 0 = 0 to avoid triggering start, bits [31:1] = 1) to 0x2C while busy_i=0, done_i=0, err_i=0; then read back 0x40 and 0x2C.
Checks: Verify that 0x40 still returns 32'h0006_0001 and 0x2C still returns 32'h0000_0000 (bits [31:1] are not overwritten by S_AXI_WDATA).
Expected_result: Writes to 0x40 and bits [31:1] of 0x2C do not alter hardware state; BRESP remains OKAY (2'b00).
Notes: Ensures accidental software writes to RO registers do not corrupt system state.
Golden_Reference_Rule: reg[0x40] always == 32'h0006_0001; reg[0x2C][0] always reads as 0.
Bug_Injection_Target: Allowing overwrites to r_hw_version or bits [3:1] of 0x2C -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: 0x40 always returns 0x00060001; 0x2C[31:1] strictly reflects {err_i, done_sticky, busy_i}.

Objective: Verify byte-strobe protection S_AXI_WSTRB[0] on registers 0x00..0x0C, 0x24, and especially the start trigger command at 0x2C.
Stimulus: After loading initial values into 0x00..0x0C and 0x24, issue new write transactions with S_AXI_WSTRB = 4'b1110 (WSTRB[0] = 0) and S_AXI_WDATA = 32'hFFFF_FFFF to 0x00..0x0C, 0x24, and 0x2C.
Checks: Verify that when S_AXI_WSTRB[0] == 0: registers 0x00..0x0C and 0x24 retain their previous values; writing to 0x2C with WDATA[0]=1 but WSTRB[0]=0 MUST NOT assert start_o and MUST NOT clear done_sticky_r.
Expected_result: No registers are modified and no start_o pulse is generated when S_AXI_WSTRB[0] == 0.
Notes: Directly tests the if (S_AXI_WSTRB[0]) condition at lines 122, 176-179, 185, and 188.
Golden_Reference_Rule: When WSTRB[0]==0: start_o == 0, and registers gated by WSTRB[0] retain their previous values.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing the S_AXI_WSTRB[0] check at line 122 or 188 -> start_o falsely triggers on upper-byte writes -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: start_o == 0 and register values are 100% preserved when WSTRB[0]=0.

Objective: Verify that writing bit 0 = 1 to register 0x2C generates an exact single-cycle pulse on start_o, and writing bit 0 = 0 to 0x2C generates no start_o pulse.
Stimulus: Write 32'h0000_0001 (WSTRB=4'hF) to 0x2C and monitor start_o cycle-by-cycle for 10 consecutive cycles. Next, write 32'h0000_0000 to 0x2C, and finally read back 0x2C.
Checks: Verify that start_o asserts to 1 for exactly 1 S_AXI_ACLK cycle and automatically deasserts to 0 on the next cycle (via line 163: start_pulse_r <= 1'b0); reading 0x2C always returns bit 0 == 0.
Expected_result: start_o is a 1-cycle-wide pulse when writing WDATA[0]=1, and remains 0 when writing WDATA[0]=0.
Notes: If start_o stays at 1 for more than 1 cycle, l2_tiling_agu will be falsely re-triggered after completing a fast job.
Golden_Reference_Rule: start_o pulse width == 1 S_AXI_ACLK cycle; RDATA(0x2C)[0] == 1'b0.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing line 163 (start_pulse_r <= 1'b0) causing start_o to stick at 1 -> TB and SVA report FAIL on the very next cycle.
Pass_Criteria: start_o==1 for exactly 1 cycle; 0 extra cycles.

Category: Done Sticky & IRQ Clear on Read
Objective: Verify the lifecycle of done_sticky_r and interrupt irq_o: latches to 1 upon receiving a done_i=1 pulse from PL, remains asserted (sticky) until PS reads register 0x2C, returning bit 2 = 1 while clearing the flag to 0 on the following cycle.
Stimulus: Pulse done_i=1 for 1 cycle from the PL side; wait 20 cycles (while reading other registers such as 0x00 and 0x40 to confirm reading non-status registers does not clear done_sticky); then perform a 1st read of 0x2C followed immediately by a 2nd read of 0x2C.
Checks: Verify that irq_o asserts to 1 immediately after the done_i=1 pulse and stays at 1 across all 20 cycles despite reads to 0x00/0x40; on the 1st read of 0x2C, S_AXI_RDATA[2] must be 1; immediately after the 0x2C read is accepted, done_sticky_r and irq_o deassert to 0 so the 2nd read of 0x2C returns S_AXI_RDATA[2] == 0.
Expected_result: Reading other registers does not clear done_sticky; the 1st read of 0x2C observes bit 2 = 1 and clears the flag; the 2nd read of 0x2C observes bit 2 = 0 and irq_o = 0.
Notes: This Clear-on-Read (COR) mechanism is critical so the C++ driver only needs a single 0x2C read to both check completion and acknowledge the interrupt.
Golden_Reference_Rule: First 0x2C read after done_i returns bit 2 = 1, after which done_sticky_r=0 and irq_o=0.
Bug_Injection_Target: Clearing done_sticky_r before latching S_AXI_RDATA[2] (or omitting axi_araddr_r[7:2]==6'h0B at line 125) -> PS reading 0x2C always sees bit 2 = 0 or loses done on other reads -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: 1st read: RDATA[2]==1; afterwards irq_o==0 and 2nd read: RDATA[2]==0.

Category: Done Sticky Clear on New Start
Objective: Verify the second clear path for done_sticky_r: when done_sticky_r is currently 1 (PS does not read 0x2C and instead issues a new start command directly by writing bit 0 = 1 to 0x2C), done_sticky_r and irq_o must clear to 0.
Stimulus: Pulse done_i=1 so done_sticky_r=1 and irq_o=1; without reading 0x2C, write 32'h0000_0001 directly to 0x2C to issue a new start; then read 0x2C.
Checks: Verify that immediately after the cycle writing the new start (write_start_pulse_now_w=1 at line 133), done_sticky_r and irq_o drop to 0.
Expected_result: Writing a new start clears the stale done_sticky flag; writing bit 0 = 0 to 0x2C does NOT clear done_sticky.
Notes: Prevents a newly started job from seeing a lingering done_sticky=1 from the previous job, which would trick the driver into thinking the new job already finished.
Golden_Reference_Rule: write_start_pulse_now_w == 1 => done_sticky_r <= 0 on the next cycle.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing write_start_pulse_now_w from line 133 -> after starting a new job without reading status first, irq_o remains stuck at 1 -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: irq_o drops to 0 immediately after writing start=1; remains at 1 if only writing bit 0 = 0.

Objective: Verify the same-cycle collision corner case: a done_i=1 pulse from PL arrives on the EXACT same cycle that PS is reading 0x2C (read_status_now_w=1) or writing start (write_start_pulse_now_w=1).
Stimulus: Align the done_i=1 pulse to coincide with the exact cycle where (S_AXI_ARREADY && S_AXI_ARVALID && !S_AXI_RVALID) occurs at address 0x2C.
Checks: Verify the priority structure if (!ARESETN) ... else if (done_i) done_sticky_r <= 1'b1; else if (write_start || read_status) done_sticky_r <= 1'b0 at lines 129-135: done_i takes higher priority so done_sticky_r is not lost and latches to 1.
Expected_result: A hardware completion pulse done_i from PL is never swallowed by a coincident polling read from the CPU.
Notes: If the clear branch (read_status_now_w) had higher priority than the set branch (done_i), a CPU polling 0x2C on the exact cycle PL finishes would read the old value (0) while simultaneously clearing done_i, hanging the system forever!
Golden_Reference_Rule: When (done_i && read_status_now_w) occur in the same cycle: done_sticky_r on the next cycle must == 1'b1.
Bug_Injection_Target: Swapping else if (done_i) below else if (read_status_now_w) at lines 131-135 -> done_i pulse is swallowed on coincident CPU polling -> TB catches this deadlock bug immediately.
Pass_Criteria: done_sticky_r == 1 and irq_o == 1 after the collision cycle.

Objective: Verify live reflection of input status signals busy_i (bit 1) and err_i (bit 3) from PL onto register 0x2C across all 8 combinations of {err_i, done_sticky, busy_i}.
Stimulus: Sequentially set all 8 combinations of {err_i, done_sticky_r, busy_i} = 3'b000 .. 3'b111 and read register 0x2C.
Checks: Verify that S_AXI_RDATA[3:0] returns {err_i, done_sticky_r, busy_i, 1'b0} and S_AXI_RDATA[31:4] == 28'd0.
Expected_result: All 8 status combinations are accurately reflected at their exact bit positions in register 0x2C.
Notes: Ensures the bit concatenation order {28'b0, err_i, done_sticky_r, busy_i, 1'b0} at line 239 matches kr260_npu_driver.h.
Bug_Injection_Target: Swapping err_i and busy_i positions at line 239 -> TB reports status bit mismatch.

Category: AXI4-Lite Write Channel Skew & BREADY Stall
Objective: Verify AXI4-Lite Write protocol under 3 phase-skew scenarios: (1) AWVALID arrives 1..5 cycles before WVALID; (2) WVALID arrives 1..5 cycles before AWVALID; (3) Master holds BREADY=0 for 10 cycles after BVALID=1.
Stimulus: Perform writes to registers 0x00..0x3C under all 3 skew scenarios above and verify handshake signals AWREADY, WREADY, BVALID, and BRESP.
Checks: Verify that the slave asserts AWREADY=1 and WREADY=1 only when both AWVALID and WVALID are present (line 165); when BVALID=1 and BREADY=0, BVALID and BRESP=2'b00 remain stable until BREADY=1; written register data is accurate.
Expected_result: AXI4-Lite Write handshake complies with the AMBA specification under all AW/W skew and BREADY back-pressure conditions.
Notes: The AXI SmartConnect interconnect on Zynq UltraScale+ frequently asserts AWVALID and WVALID skewed by 1-2 cycles.
Golden_Reference_Rule: Write transaction completes with BRESP=2'b00; target register latches the exact new data.
Bug_Injection_Target: Latching axi_awaddr_r before WVALID is present or dropping BVALID before BREADY=1 -> SVA and TB report AXI-Lite protocol violation.
Pass_Criteria: 0 AXI-Lite protocol errors; 100% accurate register values.

Category: AXI4-Lite Read RREADY Back-Pressure on Status
Objective: Verify AXI4-Lite Read protocol when Master holds RREADY=0 while RVALID=1 for multiple cycles, specifically when reading register 0x2C (which triggers clearing of done_sticky_r).
Stimulus: Pulse done_i=1 so done_sticky_r=1; issue a read to 0x2C (ARVALID=1) but hold S_AXI_RREADY=0 for 8 cycles after S_AXI_RVALID=1 before asserting S_AXI_RREADY=1.
Checks: Verify that throughout all 8 cycles where RVALID=1 && RREADY=0, S_AXI_RDATA[2] (done_sticky) latched as 1 on the first cycle REMAINS 1 until RREADY=1 (even though the internal done_sticky_r register was already cleared to 0 on the cycle the read began!).
Expected_result: S_AXI_RDATA holds {err, 1'b1, busy, 1'b0} stably across all 8 cycles waiting for RREADY=1; it does not drop to 0 mid-handshake when done_sticky_r clears.
Notes: Sharp corner case: if S_AXI_RDATA were assigned combinationally from done_sticky_r instead of latched into S_AXI_RDATA when (!S_AXI_RVALID), a 1-cycle RREADY delay would cause the Master to read done_sticky=0 (losing the completion flag entirely)!
Bug_Injection_Target: Updating S_AXI_RDATA every cycle without the !S_AXI_RVALID guard at line 224 -> on the 2nd cycle of RREADY=0, S_AXI_RDATA[2] drops from 1 to 0 -> TB catches the bug immediately.
Pass_Criteria: S_AXI_RDATA[2] stays stably at 1 until RVALID && RREADY completes.

Objective: Verify concurrent handling of a Write transaction (AW/W/B channels) and a Read transaction (AR/R channels) occurring in the exact same clock cycle.
Stimulus: Simultaneously assert AWVALID=1, WVALID=1 (writing to register A, or writing start to 0x2C) and ARVALID=1 (reading from register B, or reading 0x2C/0x40) in the same clock cycle.
Checks: Verify that both the Write FSM and Read FSM respond independently without deadlocking or corrupting each other's axi_awaddr_r / axi_araddr_r addresses.
Expected_result: Both concurrent Read and Write transactions complete on time with OKAY (2'b00) responses and accurate data.
Notes: The independent Write FSM (line 139) and Read FSM (line 209) must be verified to have no conflicts on done_sticky_r.
Golden_Reference_Rule: Write and Read channels operate completely independently.
Bug_Injection_Target: Sharing a single address variable for both read and write -> concurrent read/write corrupts address decoding -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: 100% of simultaneous transactions complete without error.

Objective: Verify address decode behavior when accessing unmapped offsets (0x44 to 0xFC) within the 8-bit address space.
Stimulus: Write 32'hFFFF_FFFF to addresses 0x44, 0x48, 0x80, and 0xFC; then read from these addresses and read back all 17 valid registers 0x00..0x40.
Checks: Verify that reading from an unmapped address always returns 32'h0000_0000 (default branch at line 245) with RRESP=2'b00 (preventing AXI bus hang); writing to an unmapped address is ignored (default branch at line 194) and does not modify any valid register.
Expected_result: The AXI bus responds with OKAY (2'b00), reads return 0, and all 17 valid registers retain their previous values.
Notes: Without a default branch returning BVALID/RVALID, the ARM CPU AXI4-Lite bus would hang permanently on an out-of-range offset read.
Bug_Injection_Target: Removing the default branch at line 245 (retaining previous S_AXI_RDATA) -> reading 0x44 leaks stale data -> TB reports FAIL.
Pass_Criteria: All reads to addresses > 0x40 return 32'h0; 0 side effects.

Objective: Run a 10,000-transaction constrained-random AXI4-Lite Read/Write stress test combined with randomized PL status inputs (busy_i, done_i, err_i) checked against a cycle-accurate Register Mirror Scoreboard.
Stimulus: Execute 10,000 randomized steps driven by seed (+SEED=): randomly select Read, Write, or simultaneous Read+Write, random address 0x00..0x50, random WSTRB, random AW/W/BREADY/RREADY delays, and random done_i/busy_i/err_i pulses.
Checks: After every cycle, compare all cfg_*_o, start_o, irq_o ports and S_AXI_RDATA read values against the Register Mirror Golden Model cycle-by-cycle.
Expected_result: All 10,000 transactions match the reference model 100%; 0 SVA errors; 100% functional coverage achieved.
Notes: Guarantees the register interface block has no hidden state bugs under arbitrary software access sequences.
Golden_Reference_Rule: Cycle-accurate bit-exact match against the Register Mirror Model.
Bug_Injection_Target: Any corner-case bug in the AXI-Lite FSMs or done_sticky logic is exposed across 10,000 randomized steps.
